hypothesis: Contrastive Learning is applied to detect reward hacking by training agents to distinguish between natural and manipulated reward signals, thereby improving efficiency in reinforcement learning systems
description: This method learns robust representations by emphasizing differences between normal and hacked reward patterns, allowing the agent to generalize beyond specific exploits; by focusing on the structure of reward interactions rather than their content, it may reduce susceptibility to deceptive behaviors without requiring extensive retraining or human oversight
